title: Sliding-window correction for delayed usage events in per-model console charts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: We observe persistent out-of-order and delayed ingestion of usage events from the ingestion pipeline (~1-72 hours) that causes per-model and per-route charts in the Console to show large retroactive spikes after nightly backfills. This ticket implements a sliding-window reconciliation strategy and conservative chart smoothing so frontend charts and cost attributions remain accurate and predictable while backfills complete.

Symptoms and impact: Console customers see sudden token/embedding usage spikes that do not match their application telemetry. This triggers support tickets, billing confusion, and false regressions in our quality and cost dashboards. Recent incidents: 2026-02-24 pipeline incident increased delayed events from our EU region by ~18%, exposing issues in quota enforcement and rate-limiter counters when retroactive events arrive.

Root cause analysis:
- Primary: The ingestion buffer writes to the per-customer time-series out-of-order during transient broker lag; our consolidation job treats late events as immediate increments to daily totals, causing visible spikes.
- Secondary: Rate-limiter counters (leaky-bucket) and quota burn tracking are recorded in the ingress tier and sometimes reprocessed by backfill jobs, leading to double-counting unless reconciled.
- Edge: Embeddings tokenization and generation token counts use different event schemas; backfills for embeddings had a different event key, so attributions were split across two model keys before mapping was applied.

Proposed solution (high-level):
1) Sliding-window reconciliation: Maintain a 7-day correction window for per-customer per-model timeseries. When a late event arrives for timestamp T, apply a correction delta to the storage layer rather than incrementing the current day's aggregates. Corrections are labeled as "backfill_adjustment" and include original_event_id for auditability.
2) Idempotent dedupe: Use canonical event hashing (customer, model_id, request_id, event_type, token_signature) to skip or reconcile duplicates created by replays.
3) Rate-limiter reconciliation: Preserve an authoritative quota ledger at the quota-service (single-writer per-customer per-period). Backfill processors will write to a reconciliation queue that the quota-service consumes to adjust burned tokens and record a reconciliation entry rather than modifying live counters directly.
4) Chart smoothing and UX: Console will show a translucent band for the reconciliation window (configurable up to 14 days) and an option to "Include backfills". By default, the time-series visualizes a 24–72 hour rolling average for windows inside the reconciliation period to reduce surprise spikes.
5) Migration for embedding/generation split: Add a mapping layer in the backfill pipeline to normalize older event keys to the current model-id taxonomy before applying corrections.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (Spike, 2 days): Prototype correction delta writes in dev with sample late event stream and create unit tests for idempotent dedupe.
- M2 (Core work, 6 days): Implement reconciliation queue consumer in quota-service, add correction metadata to time-series store (influx/tsdb shim), and add canonical hashing module.
- M3 (Frontend, 3 days, parallel): Add reconciliation band and "Include backfills" toggle; add explanatory tooltip.
- M4 (Backfill job updates, 2 days): Patch existing nightly backfill jobs to emit reconciliation entries rather than direct aggregate writes.
- M5 (Rollout & monitoring, 2 days): Gradual rollout to staging then canary customers with monitoring dashboards and automated alerts for reconciliation volume anomalies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console per-model daily totals do not increase >5% retroactively for events older than 72 hours after rollout for the next 14 days when compared to an authoritative ledger sample.
- No duplicate increment events after canonical dedupe in >=95% of test replays.
- Quota-service shows explicit reconciliation entries and reconciled burned tokens match corrected aggregates within a 0.5% tolerance for sampled customers.
- Frontend displays the reconciliation band when enabled and toggling "Include backfills" re-renders charts deterministically.

Monitoring and observability:
- New metrics: reconciliation.volumes.{region,customer}, reconciliation.dedupe.rate, reconciliation.delta_error_rate.
- Alerts: reconciliation.volumes spike, reconciliation.dedupe.rate < 90% for 1 hour, reconciliation.delta_error_rate > 1%.
- Dashboard: Reconciliation audit view for support to inspect original_event_id, canonical_hash, and before/after aggregates.

Rollout notes and canary plan:
- Start with internal data team and 3 low-risk customers (staging-like usage patterns) for 48 hours.
- If no anomalies, broaden to 10% traffic for 7 days, comparing reconciliation totals with pre-rollover snapshots.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Additional read/write complexity on time-series store may increase latency for real-time dashboards. Mitigation: Make correction writes async and pre-aggregate in the reconciliation table; frontend queries combine base aggregates and corrections in a single fetch.
- Risk: Misaligned schemas cause mapping failures for legacy events. Mitigation: Add fallback heuristics and retain original payload in reconciliation entries for manual recovery.
- Risk: Users may be confused by banding UX. Mitigation: Provide inline help and an audit trail link to the raw reconciliation entries.

Follow-ups (post-launch):
- 30-day postmortem to evaluate residual backfill volumes and UX confusion metrics.
- Export a reconciliation report for billing team to validate monthly invoices.
- Investigate trimming reconciliation window to 72 hours after observed stability.
